lexicalDispositions.disposition: Candidate necessary native-word support; not authored or accepted.
lexicalDispositions.evidence: 隼 はやぶさ is the falcon noun, especially peregrine falcon. The noun sense is marked usually kana; the katakana ハヤブサ reading has re_nokanji. Spelling and hiragana-reading priorities news1/nf24 are preserved independently. This is a lexical noun, not a name-only field.
lexicalDispositions.pending: Verify the exact Japanese はやぶさ/隼 heading, useful modern examples and quiz label scope. Prefer one words/隼.md primary はやぶさ article if necessary; no source-derived JLPT vocabulary level or separate katakana loanword card. Do not claim every use identifies the peregrine species.

lexicalDispositions.disposition: Complete technical family retained; no extra support commitment.
lexicalDispositions.evidence: 隼科 はやぶさか / ハヤブサ科 ハヤブサか denotes Falconidae. Each reading is restricted to its corresponding spelling.
lexicalDispositions.pending: Not needed merely to fill a reading table. Preserve spelling-specific restrictions if used; a family name does not establish all Japanese common bird names as strict scientific categories.

lexicalDispositions.disposition: Candidate シュン allocation anchor with explicit archaic boundary.
lexicalDispositions.evidence: 鷹隼 ようしゅん means hawk and falcon and is marked archaic. The complete family catches 隼 non-initially. Combined with source readings, the final しゅん is a candidate character allocation, not an everyday-vocabulary recommendation.
lexicalDispositions.pending: Inspect an exact Japanese 鷹隼 heading and reading before teaching allocation/register. Do not call this compound common or create a support article/question only to force every metadata reading into practice.

lexicalDispositions.disposition: Specialized bird identities retained, not necessary-support additions.
lexicalDispositions.evidence: 稚児隼 ちごはやぶさ denotes northern hobby; 白隼 しろはやぶさ denotes gyrfalcon. Both senses are usually kana; katakana readings carry re_nokanji. They demonstrate the native sequence in compounds, not the on-readings or ordinary unqualified falcon-species equivalence.
lexicalDispositions.pending: No extra bird cards or invented examples to fill quota. Reconsider only if genuinely useful in the bounded はやぶさ explanation.

lexicalDispositions.disposition: Plant-name family retained; no compositional falcon gloss.
lexicalDispositions.evidence: 隼人瓜/隼人うり はやとうり is chayote, usually kana; ハヤトウリ is re_nokanji. The word's はやと sequence is not evidence for whole 隼 はやぶさ, シュン or ジュン.
lexicalDispositions.pending: Do not infer a per-character はや reading, invent a falcon-fruit etymology or add a plant article without need.

lexicalDispositions.disposition: Historical lexical family retained separately from nanori.
lexicalDispositions.evidence: 隼人 has はやと/はいと and obsolete-kana はやひと. The first sense is the historical Hayato ethnic group in ancient Kyushu; the second 'man from Kagoshima' sense is restricted to はやと. This noun entry is not the same as raw KANJIDIC2 nanori はや.
lexicalDispositions.pending: No historical/ethnic or personal-name expansion. Do not copy the restricted second sense to はいと, use whole-word readings as isolated 隼 metadata, or label all lexical uses name-only.

comparisonDispositions.disposition: Bird-label and quiz-overlap evidence; no new comparison article commitment.
comparisonDispositions.evidence: 鷹 たか has hawk AND falcon glosses and usual-kana notation; 鷲 わし is eagle. 鳥/鶏/禽 とり includes bird and food senses, with esp. 鶏 a sense note and 禽 rare-spelling flag, not unrestricted aliases. 雀 すずめ also has talkative/knowledgeable-person senses. Existing 鷹 card and word titles are 'hawk; falcon'; 鳥 is the broader category.
comparisonDispositions.pending: Do not use 鷹 or 鳥 as wrong falcon-label choices or assert exclusive hawk-versus-falcon taxonomy. Plan direct exclusions on any new support, including actual displayed 鷹/鳥 labels and any additional broad-category articles found at draft time. Shared exclusions are not transitive. 鷲/雀 have no current cards; leave qualified plain text if mentioned, without expanding membership.

comparisonDispositions.disposition: Radical/shape navigation, not historical or phonetic derivation.
comparisonDispositions.evidence: 隹 ふるとり is the radical-name family; raw KANJIDIC2 gives 隼 radical172 隹 and ten strokes. 集 しゅう is a collection suffix, 準 じゅん a semi/quasi prefix. Existing 集 has 木 beneath 隹; 準 has water marks and a lower 十. These word readings do not independently establish 隼 シュン or ジュン.
comparisonDispositions.pending: Use a labelled modern-shape mnemonic and structure-unclassified unless exact historical evidence is separately inspected. Do not infer that the visible 十 means 'ten falcons', or that 準's ジュン transfers automatically to 隼. Candidate wrong meanings gather/standard/ten require final semantic review, not only visual resemblance.

comparisonDispositions.disposition: Complete independent 十 families retained; no source metadata change.
comparisonDispositions.evidence: The numerical 十 family includes alternate spellings, reading restrictions, legal-document 拾 note, とお-only age sense and 什-only archaic poetry-book sense. Separate 十 シー is a Chinese-origin numerical word. Existing words/十.md primarily teaches じゅう, not シー.
comparisonDispositions.pending: Compare the visible lower 十 only. Do not treat whole-word Chinese シー as sourced 隼 metadata or retrofit existing 十 teaching from this inspection.

comparisonDispositions.disposition: Lexical-boundary guard for 速, not a speed etymology.
comparisonDispositions.evidence: Exact standalone 速 そく here is a gear/speed suffix-counter. Existing kanji/速.md teaches the fast character and links 速い, a different lexical identity not extracted by this exact-spelling comparison selection.
comparisonDispositions.pending: No claim that this family establishes 速い はやい or an etymology of はやぶさ. If draft wording needs speed/early comparisons, extract and inspect the actual complete word families and reused articles first.

comparisonDispositions.disposition: Distinct kana-only spacecraft identity retained outside the falcon lexical packet.
comparisonDispositions.evidence: はやぶさ is independently entered as the Japanese Hayabusa spacecraft, with a cross-reference to the falcon noun. The reference is not an unrestricted kanji spelling permission.
comparisonDispositions.pending: Do not merge spacecraft and ordinary animal senses into a new word card, or use the spacecraft to prove general bird collocations.
